fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled fuzz input bytes (>=100, here 100) arrive as the Ruby String ruby_xml; its byte length + 1 becomes len, the exact size of the copy buffer.
For len <= SMALL_XML (4096) the XML working copy is a variable-length array on the stack, exactly len bytes (indices 0..len-1).
Copies input bytes plus a trailing NUL into the stack buffer; the buffer is exactly len bytes so any byte read at xml[len] is out of bounds.
Parser receives buffer start and length len-1; pi->end is placed at the terminating NUL.
pi->end points at the NUL terminator (the last byte of the ALLOCA buffer); pi->s walks through the input until it hits this NUL.
Top-level '<a>' is dispatched to read_element; the element name is consumed and '>' sets hasChildren=1 so the children/text loop runs.
After '<a>' the rest of the input is plain text (no '<'), so read_element delegates to read_text starting at the first text byte.
read_text consumes bytes one at a time; when pi->s reaches the NUL at pi->end the post-increment advances pi->s to pi->end + 1, one byte past the stack buffer.

fine_trace.code: case '\0': set_error(&pi->err, "invalid format, document not terminated", pi->str, pi->s); return;
fine_trace.note: The one-past-the-end pointer pi->s (pi->end + 1, i.e. xml + len) is forwarded as `current`; the safety condition pi->s <= pi->end that should have held is violated.

fine_trace.note: The macro passes the out-of-bounds pointer unchanged as `current` into _ox_err_set_with_location.
